records.issue_text: No check for `eventType.disableGuests` (or equivalent event-type-level policy) before allowing this mutation, which would let this endpoint bypass an organizer's explicit configuration disallowing extra guests on that event type.

records.issue_text: There is no upper bound on the number of guests that can be added in one call; combined with the missing test coverage, this leaves room for abuse (mass-adding attendees to spam their inboxes with calendar invites).

The UI (`MultiEmail`) lets users add unlimited fields, and the handler does `createMany` plus sends emails per attendee in `sendAddGuestsEmails`, enabling potential mass-add/spam abuse in a single call. records.issue_text: Silent dropping of blacklisted/duplicate emails: the caller has no way to know which of their submitted emails were filtered out vs. actually added (`{ message: "Guests added" }` doesn't report this), which could look like a bug from the UI end when someone expects N guests added but fewer show up.
records.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the server filters submitted `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by removing already-existing attendee emails and blacklisted emails (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). It only errors when *all* are filtered (`if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw ...`), but on partial filtering it still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the UI always toasts `t("guests_added")` on success.
